reuse.why: Extends the existing shared getScheduledAmount, reuses getApproxNumberThreshold for the matching tolerance, and moves the budget template from its own isbetween ternary onto getScheduledAmount.

duplication.why: The approximate worst case is defined once (getApproximateWorstCaseAmount inside getScheduledAmount); call sites only pass their operator.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts beside the ranged worst case, where every server and client consumer already resolves schedule amounts.

scope.why: Every getScheduledAmount caller is threaded with its operator, including display-only list and table cells, which goes a little beyond planning but keeps all consumers consistent.

maintainability.why: One definition for all consumers is easy to own; the optional loosely typed op after a positional inverse boolean (every caller writes 'false, op') means a new caller that omits it silently gets the exact value.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All planning consumers (budget template, forecast, preview transactions, post-transaction, API expectedAmount, balances) go through getScheduledAmount; the template's direct getWorstCaseAmount use is removed.

disguised_duplication.where: No duplicated logic; the per-caller edits only pass the operator.

one_place.where: getScheduledAmount (with getApproximateWorstCaseAmount) in packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts, called by every code path that resolves a schedule's expected amount.
